note: Deep screen of the p60 ideas at record-search scale: each idea switched on in the seed configuration with centrosymmetric on, 150 seeds (7000 to 7149) x n23, n26, n28, n31 at 240 CPU-seconds. Baseline: the control arm.

arms.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
arms.hypothesis: Since every axis plane x = c, y = c, z = c holds at most 4 points, a large set must be spread evenly over the layers, so refilling with the sampled free point whose three axis planes hold the fewest members (best of layer_balance_m samples) keeps the layers balanced and leaves room for more points.

arms.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
arms.hypothesis: Each ruin costs a full pass over the incidence records and the grid while a tentative refill is cheap, so refilling the same hole multi_recreate_m times and keeping the largest refill (ties: the one with the most new points) gets several search attempts, and more real plateau moves, per expensive ruin.

arms.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
arms.hypothesis: Keeping a per-member count of incidences at every grid point, plus a chain of records per grid point, lets a ruin find the freed points without moving the removed members' records out of the record array and back, so a rejected step (the common case) no longer makes two passes over the whole array and more steps fit in the same CPU time.

arms.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
arms.hypothesis: A one-step tabu on reinsertion: after a ruin the refill first places only free points that were not just removed, and the removed points fill what room is left, so a step with any fresh free point is a real exchange instead of usually putting the same points back, and the search walks its plateau much faster.

arms.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
arms.hypothesis: An axis plane x = c, y = c or z = c holds at most 4 members and a plane with 4 is blocked as a whole, so a ruin that removes every member of one random axis plane (instead of random members) reopens that layer jointly and lets the refill repack it from scratch, an exchange that scattered random removals almost never make.

arms.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
arms.hypothesis: A tabu on revisiting: free points that left the set within the last revisit_tenure accepted moves are refilled last, after the fresh and the just-removed points, so the plateau walk stops paying an expensive sphere enumeration to step straight back to a set it has just left and covers new sets instead.

arms.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
arms.hypothesis: Seeding the search with a centrosymmetric phase (the construction and the first symmetric_start_frac of the budget build a set of antipodal pairs, then the symmetry is dropped and the ordinary search continues from that set) should help because the symmetric search space is half the size and climbs quickly to a high plateau, which the unrestricted search can then extend with unpaired points.

arms.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
arms.hypothesis: The refill tests every candidate against all C(k,3) triples of the tentative set, but the spheres through old members were already enumerated at commit time, so reading the saved incidence records for old triples and doing geometry only for triples that contain a freshly placed point finds the same blocked points at a fraction of the cost, and more steps fit in the same CPU time.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: A rejected step is the common case and currently rewrites the whole incidence-record array twice (compact the survivors, push the removed ones back), so lowering the counters with a read-only scan, backing them up, and compacting the records only when the step is accepted makes the same search run more steps per CPU second.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Removing a spatially compact cluster of members (a random member and its nearest neighbours) for kicks and some ruins reopens one region of the cube jointly, so the refill repacks it from scratch, an exchange that scattered random removals almost never make.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Removing a member drawn in proportion to the number of blocking spheres it belongs to (by sampling a random incidence record) frees the most grid points per removal, so each ruin targets the most constraining part of the set instead of a random member.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: A kick that removes the members nearest a random grid point opens one connected hole whose repacking is a coherent local re-solve, whereas a kick of the same size scattered over the whole cube mostly just refills the old points.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Sliding one member to a nearby lattice point (remove it, force a random neighbour in first) is a small structured exchange that keeps the rest of the near-optimal arrangement intact, so the plateau walk makes more productive moves than blind random removal.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: A kick that first rebuilds the best set found so far and then ruins a quarter of it restarts the search from the strongest known construction instead of from wherever the plateau walk has drifted, so each basin is explored around the best set rather than around a drifted one.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: At a kick, returning with some probability to a snapshot of the best set found so far (rather than kicking the drifted current set) keeps restarts rooted in the best basin, so the plateau walk after each kick explores around the best set instead of wandering away from it.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: A ruin that frees no point except the removed ones changes nothing and stays that way until the set changes, so remembering such dead ruins (hashed by the removed ids, cleared whenever the set changes) lets repeats skip the record-array passes and the free-point scan, and more real steps fit in the same CPU time.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Building the set from pairs related by a half turn about the cube's z axis (instead of the antipodal map) halves the search space while filling each z layer two points at a time, a symmetry compatible with the 4-per-layer limit and not yet tried on n >= 17, where the antipodal symmetry is not what the records have.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: At a kick, first return the current set to the best set found so far, so the kick perturbs the best basin instead of whatever the downhill acceptance has drifted to.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Registering a new member scans all n^2 (x, y) pairs for every member triple, but a sphere only occupies its bounding box, so scanning only the box (and per x the circle's y range) finds the same records in the same order with fewer lookups, and more steps fit in the same CPU time.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Preferring refill points whose antipode about the cube centre is already in the set builds a soft centrosymmetry (the published n = 13 to 16 records are fully antipodal) without the hard pairing, so symmetric sub-structure accumulates while unpaired points stay allowed.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Placing the outermost of a few sampled free points first (a tournament on distance from the cube centre) fills the cube boundary before the interior, since outer points share fewer spheres with other grid points and block fewer free points, so the refill packs more points.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Kicks that fail to improve the best set escalate in size (kick_fraction grows by kick_escalate_step per fruitless kick, reset on a new best), so a deep basin that small kicks cannot leave is eventually abandoned while fresh basins still get gentle kicks.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: The commit scan tests all n^2 (x, y) cells for every member triple, but the target value must lie within the min/max range of the fz values, so skipping whole x rows and single cells whose target is out of range (the same records in the same order) saves lookups and more steps fit in the same CPU time.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: A grid point blocked by exactly two spheres can be freed by removing one member of each; inserting it first makes a 2-for-1 plateau exchange that the single-sphere guided ruin and random removals rarely reach, so the walk escapes plateaus that single exchanges cannot.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Ruin sizes ramp from ruin_max up to ruin_max + ruin_ramp_extra as steps without a new best approach patience, so a basin that small exchanges cannot leave is attacked with progressively bigger ruins before the kick, while a fresh basin still polishes with small ruins.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Forcing in the image of a member under a random cube symmetry (axis permutation and flips), and removing a member of the one sphere that blocks it, proposes exchanges that echo the set's approximate symmetry, so they should be more productive than blind random exchanges.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Translating (and flipping) the whole set at a kick keeps all its near-optimal local structure but pushes a boundary slab out of the cube and opens the opposite slab, so the refill re-solves only the edge region instead of a random scatter, a structured large move unlike random-removal kicks.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Laying down the points of random modular polynomial curves (x, y(x) mod n, z(x) mod n) first starts the search from a spread-out, algebraically structured set that random greedy filling rarely reaches, so the plateau walk starts from a better basin.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: The commit scan, the dominant cost of an accepted step, hashes every lookup with a 64-bit multiply, but after dividing the common power of two out of the surface values the low byte is already a good hash, so the same records are found with one fewer multiply per lookup and more steps fit in the same CPU time.

arms.author: llm:claude-sonnet-5-5
arms.hypothesis: Building the initial set and refilling after kicks in two passes, first only with points whose three axis planes hold fewer than latin_cap members and then freely, spreads the points evenly over the layers (each holds at most 4) and gives the search a more balanced starting basin than a purely random greedy fill.

arms.author: seed
arms.hypothesis: A/A control: the seed solver with centrosymmetric on, run again on the same seeds
